product.title: the B6 integration of the shared files

pending.claim: The reservation credit reads 'TIGER/Line 2026 (reservations and roads)', but the next sentence (line 56) takes place names from the TIGER 2026 place file. D130(c) says the TIGER credit line covers place names ('reservations, roads and place names').
pending.evidence: about.html:55 and :56; the built base.json vector credit list has the same reservations-and-roads wording.
pending.fix: Change the TIGER credit to '(reservations, roads and place names)' in the About page and in the basemap2 credit line it draws from.

pending.claim: The monthly terrain verify is killed at 300 s, but terrain verify re-fetches 10 tiles one after another (terrain.py verify loop, about lines 1267 to 1276), each up to 60 s with up to three tries. A slow service, the condition the monthly build already struggles with, can time the check out; the step then marks a sound terrain layer unavailable, a false negative rather than wrong data.
pending.evidence: Line 1255: timeout --kill-after=30 300 python -m website.terrain verify ... --timeout 60; terrain.py verify iterates picks sequentially through _refetch_compare.
pending.fix: Re-fetch in parallel (the --procs setting) or lower the monthly sample, set the step timeout above the worst case, and make the log say that a timed-out check is not checked.

pending.claim: DECISIONS records D107 to D127 only. The D128 to D130 rulings (2026-10-26, 09:45 to 10:20 UTC, on the first integrators and the About and CONTRACTS integrator) are not recorded.
pending.evidence: The last B6 bullet is D127 (line 1047).
pending.fix: Add D128 to D130 as bullets in the D38 round's style when the post-integration round lands.

pending.claim: The monthly terrain verify can be killed by its own 300 s timeout, and the kill removes the month's terrain layers.
pending.evidence: verify re-fetches its 10-tile sample one after another (website/terrain.py:1271, 'for rel in picks'). Each re-fetch allows 60 s per try and up to three tries (TRIES=3, terrain.py:160; retry loop 549-564). A slow service can run past `timeout --kill-after=30 300`. Exit 124 leaves `verified` unset, so the mark step (line 1266) runs `terrain unavailable` and removes the layers for the month.
pending.fix: Give the monthly verify a budget that fits its sample (for example a 4-tile sample in the monthly job, or the remaining clock), and report a re-fetch that timed out as 'not checked' rather than failing the whole layer.

pending.claim: The printed heat legend still uses the superseded grid words.
pending.evidence: heat90_legend reads 'in cells about 4.6 km across', and built data/base.json history_layers.pictures.heat90.words.legend prints it. D113(c) and D130(a) require 'about 1/24 degree cells (roughly 4.6 by 3 km in Montana)' in every printed grid sentence; the About (about.html:91) already uses that wording, so the page contradicts itself.
pending.fix: Change heat90_legend to the ruled wording in the P4 post-integration round, and add a test that the legend carries '1/24 degree' and not '4.6 km across'.

pending.claim: The map.json headroom the supervisor relies on (590 bytes, D128(d)) does not reproduce from the store copy.
pending.evidence: Task 1 measures 163,250 bytes for the history-only build of the adopted store (headroom 590 bytes). Task 8 measures 128,522 bytes for a history-only build of the store copy with the same flags and clock. The store copy adds only the B6 folders and the 157-byte base pointer, so the 34,728-byte gap is unexplained. The built site with --hail-addresses is 397,716 bytes; without the addresses, roads and buildings blocks (268,731 bytes) that leaves about 129,000 bytes, which supports the lower figure.
pending.fix: Re-measure the history-only build of the adopted store with the flags stated, correct task 1 and D128(d) if needed, and keep the note that D82(a) gates the history flag only.

pending.claim: After the 80-minute monthly clock, the remaining steps can run past the 110-minute job cap.
pending.evidence: Caps after the clock: terrain verify 6 minutes (300 s kill), marks 5 minutes each, basemap verify 6 minutes, manifest 10, pack 5, publish 10. The worst case is about 47 minutes against about 30 minutes of headroom. Only a slow run reaches it; publish is then skipped and the last asset stays.
pending.fix: Bring the post-clock verify steps under the seconds left (cap them by LEFT), or give the monthly job more headroom.
